title: Channel Tier List: how a solopreneur ranks distribution channels from his own results
summary: Alex West ranks distribution channels A to F from a decade of trying them. He recommends launching and warm outbound first, then cold outbound and social, then long-term assets like email, YouTube and podcasts. He says channels compound together, and distribution now matters more than product.

principles.text: Distribution matters more than product, and it's only getting more important as competition rises and no new channels appear.
principles.quote: you can have a mediocre okay product average and have insane distribution uh and you can become crazy rich and improve the product over time as well

principles.text: Start with warm outbound and a launch, add cold outbound, and build inbound in parallel.
principles.quote: I always recommend start with warm out rats then add cold outre and in the meantime like build your social uh and SEO and all that other stuff

principles.text: Channels compound together rather than competing: first customers give testimonials, social proof, then inbound, which also lifts cold email replies.
principles.quote: all these channels they're not mutually exclusive like I'm doing outbound now and I'm also building my inbound and they're separate no they work together

principles.text: A launch is a strategy to get your first customers and the confidence to keep going.
principles.quote: launching is a strategy you know like you can get your first 10 customers with a launch and that's how I got my first 10 customers with cyber leads I launched on product hunt

principles.text: Cold email only fits expensive offers, and works far better when you already have a brand. A $200/month offer became $22k/month, enabling cold email.
principles.quote: it only works when you are selling expensive stuff so if you're selling like a SAS product for like $50 a month I don't think it's the best fit

principles.text: Choose the platform by customer type: B2C platforms are easy to grow but convert badly; Twitter's B2B audience is harder to grow but converts far better.
principles.quote: my business is built on a 30,000 Twitter account that's it 30,000 follower Twitter account like nothing crazy but the conversions are insane
